profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between a university emergency management research lab and a state emergency management training unit preparing a joint briefing pack for an inter-agency workshop on how AIIMS/CIMS hold up during escalating, multi-agency incidents. The pack will combine Bushfire CRC survey findings on coordination, information quality, and interoperability with practitioner-facing workshop materials for agencies in Australia and New Zealand. The agenda is to align the interface between the research synthesis stream and the training translation stream: which 'model slide' sits in the main deck, what belongs in the 'agency comparison' appendix under ethics constraints, what 'final deck by Thursday' means for each workstream, and how the incident 'examples' will be refreshed before design. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, handoffs, and timing so the workshop pack can move to design and facilitator preparation next week.

members.name: Dr. Amelia Hart
members.role: Research Lead, University Emergency Management Lab
members.expertise: Organisational coordination research, survey analysis, AIIMS/CIMS evaluation, mixed-methods synthesis
members.background: Amelia led part of the Bushfire CRC follow-on research and now works with emergency services agencies to translate coordination findings into policy and training materials without overstating the evidence.
members.private_state: She wants the workshop pack to preserve the nuance of the validated coordination model and avoid drifting into agency-specific claims that sit outside the ethics-approved framing; she also wants to minimize rework because her analyst is tied up on another deadline.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'model slide' they mean the validated structural model figure from the final manuscript, not the earlier simplified stakeholder diagram.

Because the survey reporting was ethics-cleared only for de-identified organisational patterns, everyone already understands that any 'agency comparison' necessarily means comparisons by service family or jurisdictional grouping rather than named agencies.

A 'final deck' in this handoff means final from the research team's side: the analytical content is locked, while formatting, notes, and delivery polish can still be added afterward by the training unit.
Updating the 'examples' means refining the wording and ordering of the existing ethics-approved generic escalation vignettes, not replacing them with named incidents.

If the training unit says it will handle the workshop framing, that naturally includes adapting the examples within the already-approved boundaries rather than changing the evidentiary basis of the pack.

members.name: Luke Bennett
members.role: Senior Capability Designer, State Emergency Management Training Unit
members.expertise: Inter-agency training design, doctrine translation, incident management exercises, workshop facilitation
members.background: Luke designs cross-agency learning products for incident controllers and regional coordination staff, and regularly turns research and policy material into workshop-ready decks, facilitator guides, and exercise prompts.
members.private_state: He wants a practical pack that facilitators can run without extra explanation and that participants from different agencies immediately recognize as grounded in real operational experience.
hidden_assumptions: The 'model slide' means the simplified practitioner-facing coordination diagram already used in prior planning conversations, because that is the one facilitators can teach from in a room.

When Amelia says 'agency comparison,' she obviously knows participants expect to locate their own organisation somehow, so the appendix will at least contain named agency snapshots or recognizable agency-level pages already suitable for workshop use.
A 'final deck' means final for the end-user: once it is returned Thursday it should be ready for design and facilitator circulation without further substantive development.

Updating the 'examples' means replacing the generic vignettes with named incidents drawn from the training unit's existing cleared case repository, since 'update' in workshop production normally means making material more concrete and operationally familiar.
If the researchers are comfortable with the overall message, they are also comfortable with the training unit grounding that message in real incident cases from its standard repository.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'use the model slide in the main deck.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the validated structural equation model figure from the final manuscript, lightly reformatted for presentation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the simplified coordination diagram from an earlier stakeholder workshop that translates the constructs into practitioner language.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts have circulated before, both are routinely referred to as 'the model slide,' and in a coordination meeting this sounds like a settled packaging detail rather than something needing explicit disambiguation.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'agency comparison' appendix
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include 'the agency comparison in an appendix.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this appendix will contain de-identified comparison pages by agency type and jurisdictional cluster, because she presupposes Luke already knows the ethics constraints rule out naming specific agencies.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes it will include named agency snapshots or similarly recognizable agency-level pages, because from a workshop design perspective an 'agency comparison' appendix is where users expect to see their own organisation reflected.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds administratively straightforward, and Amelia treats the anonymity boundary as already-known background while Luke treats recognizability as the obvious purpose of such an appendix, so neither hears a need to restate the boundary.

misalignment_points.topic: Definition of a 'final deck' by Thursday
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on having a 'final deck by Thursday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'final' means final for the research team: the analytical content, figures, and claims are locked by Thursday, after which the training side can still add facilitator notes, delivery framing, and design polish.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'final' means final for the end-user: by Thursday the deck should already be facilitator-ready, with examples, notes, and no remaining substantive development before circulation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a familiar local norm for the word 'final' tied to their own stage-gates, and because they are coordinating a handoff rather than negotiating content, each hears the other's deadline language as confirming the same maturity level.

misalignment_points.topic: How the incident 'examples' will be updated
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Luke will 'update the examples' before the materials go to design.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes Luke will lightly edit the existing generic escalation vignettes for readability and workshop flow while keeping the examples de-identified and within the ethics-approved research framing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes he will swap those generic vignettes out for named incidents from the training unit's own cleared case-study repository so facilitators have concrete operational references.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because Luke is not depending on Amelia for extra inputs, the handoff still sounds routine; 'update the examples' is broad enough to cover either minor editorial refinement or substitution from an existing repository, so the divergence hides inside a normal production phrase.
